title: Family Celebrations
subtitle: Celebrate birthdays and weddings, give gifts and send good wishes

lessons.title: Les fêtes de famille
lessons.description: Talk about birthdays, weddings and family gatherings, and tell the story of a celebration in the past.

blocks.heading: Naming the celebration
blocks.body: French uses une fête for almost any celebration, then adds a detail: une fête de famille, une fête surprise. The big life events have their own nouns: un anniversaire (birthday), un mariage (wedding), un baptême (christening), une naissance (birth). Notice that un anniversaire also covers a wedding anniversary — un anniversaire de mariage.

examples.french: Samedi, il y a une fête de famille chez mes parents.
examples.english: On Saturday there's a family party at my parents' place.

examples.french: C'est l'anniversaire de ma sœur : elle a vingt ans.
examples.english: It's my sister's birthday: she's turning twenty.
examples.note: French says elle a vingt ans, literally 'she has twenty years'

examples.french: Nous allons au mariage de mon cousin en juin.
examples.english: We're going to my cousin's wedding in June.

examples.french: Le baptême du bébé aura lieu à l'église.
examples.english: The baby's christening will take place at the church.

examples.french: Ils fêtent leurs trente ans de mariage.
examples.english: They're celebrating thirty years of marriage.

blocks.tip: Une fête can also mean a name day — la fête de Marie is the day of Saint Marie, and people still say Bonne fête !

blocks.heading: Fêter, célébrer, inviter
blocks.body: Fêter is the everyday verb: on fête un anniversaire. Célébrer is a little more formal and suits weddings or official events. Inviter takes a direct object for the person and à for the event: j'invite Paul à mon anniversaire. All three are regular -er verbs, so the passé composé is easy: j'ai fêté, j'ai célébré, j'ai invité.

examples.french: On fête l'anniversaire de papa dimanche.
examples.english: We're celebrating Dad's birthday on Sunday.

examples.french: Ils ont célébré leur mariage à la mairie.
examples.english: They celebrated their wedding at the town hall.

blocks.heading: How a French wedding works
blocks.body: In France the legal wedding always happens à la mairie, at the town hall, in front of the mayor. A religious ceremony à l'église is optional and comes afterwards. Then everyone moves to la réception, usually a long meal with speeches and dancing. Le marié is the groom, la mariée is the bride, and les mariés together means the newlyweds.

examples.french: Le mariage civil a lieu à la mairie à onze heures.
examples.english: The civil wedding takes place at the town hall at eleven.

examples.french: La mariée portait une longue robe blanche.
examples.english: The bride was wearing a long white dress.
examples.note: imparfait for description in the past

examples.french: Les témoins signent le registre après la cérémonie.
examples.english: The witnesses sign the register after the ceremony.

examples.french: La réception a duré jusqu'à trois heures du matin.
examples.english: The reception lasted until three in the morning.

examples.french: Mon oncle a fait un discours très drôle.
examples.english: My uncle gave a very funny speech.

blocks.tip: Each married person chooses a témoin (witness) — the closest French equivalent of a best man or maid of honour.

blocks.heading: Telling the story: passé composé vs imparfait
blocks.body: When you tell someone about a celebration, you need both past tenses. The passé composé gives the actions that moved the day forward: on est arrivés, elle a soufflé ses bougies. The imparfait paints the background — weather, mood, what things looked like, what people were wearing: il faisait beau, la salle était magnifique, tout le monde souriait.

examples.french: Il faisait beau, alors nous avons mangé dehors.
examples.english: The weather was nice, so we ate outside.

examples.french: La mariée portait une robe blanche quand elle est entrée.
examples.english: The bride was wearing a white dress when she came in.

examples.french: Tout le monde chantait pendant qu'elle coupait le gâteau.
examples.english: Everyone was singing while she was cutting the cake.

examples.french: J'ai pris beaucoup de photos parce que l'ambiance était géniale.
examples.english: I took lots of photos because the mood was great.

examples.french: Quand je suis arrivé, la fête avait déjà commencé.
examples.english: When I arrived, the party had already started.

blocks.tip: A quick test: if you could say 'was ...-ing' or 'used to' in English, French almost always wants the imparfait.

blocks.heading: Reflexive verbs in the passé composé
blocks.body: Se marier, s'amuser, se réunir and se retrouver are reflexive, so in the passé composé they take être, not avoir, and the past participle agrees with the subject. Ils se sont mariés (two men or a mixed couple), elles se sont amusées (women). Don't forget the reflexive pronoun before être: je me suis amusé.

lessons.title: Offrir un cadeau
lessons.description: Choose, give and receive presents, and use the pronouns lui and leur to say who you gave them to.

blocks.heading: Offrir, apporter, donner
blocks.body: French has three verbs where English often just says 'give'. Offrir is the one for presents — you offer someone a gift, never 'donner un cadeau' in a warm context. Apporter means to bring something with you to a place. Donner is the neutral 'hand over'. Offrir is irregular: j'offre, tu offres, il offre, nous offrons, vous offrez, ils offrent, and the past participle is offert.

examples.french: Je vais offrir un livre à ma mère.
examples.english: I'm going to give my mother a book.

examples.french: Qu'est-ce que tu as offert à Julie ?
examples.english: What did you give Julie?

examples.french: J'apporte le dessert, ne t'inquiète pas.
examples.english: I'm bringing dessert, don't worry.

examples.french: Donne-moi le paquet, s'il te plaît.
examples.english: Give me the parcel, please.

examples.french: Ils nous ont offert une très belle plante.
examples.english: They gave us a very beautiful plant.

blocks.tip: In a shop or café, C'est moi qui offre ! means 'It's on me!' — offrir also covers treating someone.

blocks.heading: Choosing the present
blocks.body: To talk about the choice itself, use chercher (to look for), choisir (to choose) and hésiter entre (to hesitate between). To say a gift suits someone, French loves the verb plaire: ça va lui plaire (he/she is going to like it). And faire plaisir à quelqu'un means to make someone happy.

examples.french: Je cherche un cadeau pour mon frère.

examples.french: J'hésite entre un parfum et un bijou.

examples.english: She's going to like this scarf a lot.
examples.note: plaire à = to be pleasing to

examples.french: J'ai choisi quelque chose d'utile et d'original.
examples.english: I chose something useful and original.

blocks.heading: Opening and thanking
blocks.body: A present arrives wrapped: dans du papier cadeau, with un ruban. You déballer (unwrap) or ouvrir (open) it, then you thank the giver. The verb is remercier quelqu'un — remercier takes a direct object, unlike dire merci à quelqu'un.

examples.french: Tu peux ouvrir ton cadeau maintenant !
examples.english: You can open your present now!

examples.french: Elle a déballé le paquet très lentement.
examples.english: She unwrapped the parcel very slowly.

examples.french: Je les ai remerciés pour leur générosité.
examples.english: I thanked them for their generosity.

examples.french: Merci beaucoup, c'est exactement ce que je voulais !
examples.english: Thank you so much, it's exactly what I wanted!

examples.french: Il ne fallait pas, c'est trop gentil.
examples.english: You shouldn't have, that's too kind.
examples.note: the standard polite reaction to a gift

blocks.tip: In France, presents are usually opened in front of the giver — it would seem cold to put the parcel aside.

blocks.heading: Indirect object pronouns: lui and leur
blocks.body: When a verb links to a person with à — offrir à quelqu'un, donner à quelqu'un, parler à quelqu'un — you can replace that person with an indirect object pronoun. Lui replaces one person (him OR her, no gender difference) and leur replaces several. Both go in front of the verb: j'offre un livre à Marie becomes je lui offre un livre. Note that leur here never takes an -s; that's only the possessive leurs.

examples.french: J'offre un livre à Marie. → Je lui offre un livre.
examples.english: I give Marie a book. → I give her a book.
examples.note: lui = to her, and also to him

blocks.tip: The full family is: me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur. Only the third person (lui / leur) differs from the direct object pronouns.

blocks.heading: Where the pronoun goes
blocks.body: In the present and the passé composé, lui and leur sit right before the conjugated verb — even the auxiliary: je lui ai offert. In the negative, ne wraps around the pronoun and the verb: je ne lui ai rien offert. With a two-verb structure like aller + infinitive or vouloir + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the infinitive: je vais lui offrir. In a positive command, it jumps behind the verb with a hyphen: donne-lui !

passages.title: Un cadeau pour Mamie
passages.french:
Ma grand-mère fête ses quatre-vingts ans dimanche prochain.
Avec mon frère, nous cherchons un cadeau depuis deux semaines.
Il voulait lui offrir un parfum, mais elle en a déjà trois.
Moi, je pensais à un bijou, seulement c'était beaucoup trop cher.
Finalement, nous avons choisi un album de photos de toute la famille.
Nous avons demandé une photo à chaque cousin et à chaque tante.
Le vendeur de la boutique a emballé l'album dans du papier doré.

lessons.title: Les vœux
lessons.description: Learn the fixed formulas for birthdays, congratulations and season's greetings, and write a card that sounds French.

blocks.heading: Bon or joyeux?
blocks.body: French good wishes are fixed phrases, and you cannot mix them freely. Bon / bonne means 'have a good ...' and pairs with most nouns: bon anniversaire, bonne année, bon voyage. Joyeux / joyeuse adds a note of joy and belongs to festive days: joyeux Noël, joyeuses Pâques, joyeux anniversaire. The adjective agrees with the noun that follows, so it is bonne année but bon anniversaire.

blocks.tip: In France you wish someone bonne année only from 1 January, and traditionally until 31 January — never before midnight on New Year's Eve.

blocks.heading: Congratulations, courage and condolences
blocks.body: Félicitations ! covers every kind of success: a wedding, a baby, an exam, a new job. When someone faces something hard, French offers bon courage (for an effort ahead) or bonne chance (for luck). If someone is ill, you say bon rétablissement, and for a death, toutes mes condoléances. These phrases stand alone — no verb needed.

blocks.heading: Writing the card
blocks.body: A French card starts with Cher / Chère + first name (Cher Paul, Chère Anna, Chers amis). The middle is the wish itself, often introduced by je te souhaite or nous vous souhaitons. Then comes a closing formula: Bises or Bisous with friends and family, Amicalement with people you know less well, Cordialement in a professional card. Finally you sign your first name.

blocks.heading: Souhaiter quelque chose à quelqu'un
blocks.body: The verb that carries most good wishes is souhaiter, and it follows the pattern souhaiter + something + à + someone. That à means you can use the indirect pronouns from the last lesson: je te souhaite, je vous souhaite, je lui souhaite, nous leur souhaitons. Use te with family and friends, vous when you are being polite or writing to more than one person.

examples.english: Wish him a speedy recovery from me.

blocks.tip: De ma part means 'from me' — a neat way to send wishes through someone else.

blocks.heading: Fixed wishes: no verb needed
blocks.body: Most French greetings are simply an adjective plus a noun, with no verb at all: bon anniversaire, bonne journée, joyeuses fêtes. The adjective must agree with the noun, and that is the only thing you have to get right. Masculine singular takes bon or joyeux; feminine singular takes bonne or joyeuse; plurals add -s or -es. You can always add pour to say what the wish is about: bon courage pour ton déménagement.

passages.french:
Chère Mamie,
Je t'écris cette carte depuis Bordeaux, où il pleut encore aujourd'hui.
Joyeux anniversaire ! Quatre-vingt-deux ans, c'est magnifique.
Je te souhaite beaucoup de bonheur et surtout une très bonne santé.
Maman m'a dit que tu prépares un grand repas pour dimanche.
Je suis vraiment triste de ne pas être là avec vous.
J'ai envoyé ton cadeau par la poste : il devrait arriver vendredi.
Ouvre-le devant tout le monde, ça leur fera plaisir aussi !
Je reviens à Nantes en juillet et je passerai te voir.
Gros bisous, Léa
